title: Income Autopilot I: Finding the Muse
coreMove: Build a muse for cash flow and owner absence: choose a reachable niche, favor products over services, price above commodity range, and keep support low.

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder judging whether product revenue is really freeing
exampleSpecs.stakes: The product is selling, but every decision still points back to the owner.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use BrainQUICKEN to separate product cash flow from owner absence.

exampleSpecs.audience: a builder choosing between broad trends and known communities
exampleSpecs.stakes: A broad trend looks attractive, but familiar communities reveal sharper demand.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use trade magazines, associations, and subscriptions to locate a reachable niche.

exampleSpecs.audience: a product owner setting price before launch
exampleSpecs.stakes: A low price feels safer but may require too many buyers and too much support.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show premium pricing reducing volume pressure and support strain.

exampleSpecs.audience: a specialist tempted to sell personal hours
exampleSpecs.stakes: Immediate service revenue may rebuild the time trap under a new name.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Favor a product when a service would resell the owner's time.

exampleSpecs.audience: a builder who understands a market but lacks full authority
exampleSpecs.stakes: The idea may stall if the founder assumes all expertise must be personal.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use expert collaboration or licensed knowledge to assemble a credible product.

exampleSpecs.audience: an entrepreneur tempted by investor-scale growth
exampleSpecs.stakes: The business may become impressive while overshooting the life it was meant to fund.
